paragraphs.text: A real browser for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI right sidebar: CDP-driven Chrome, not an iframe, wit

# Browser panel for DeepSeek Harness

A right-Sidebar **Browser** tab for the DSH Web GUI that streams a real Chrome page over
CDP, forwar

ds mouse/keyboard input, and turns a clicked page element into conversation
context — the "pick elem
ent into context" flow familiar from Cursor/opencode.

**This is the browser for the Web UI itself.** It is built for the DSH **Web** profile: the tab
rend

ers in the right Sidebar of `dsh web`, and the page behind it is a real Chrome running on the
host,

driven over CDP. That is a different thing from the `Browser` that ships with DSH
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh

-client-ui-sidebar-browser`): in a Web profile that one is a sandboxed **iframe**
(an Electron `<web

view>` on Desktop), it is switched **off by default** in Web profiles, and it is a
viewer — no CDP,

no agent tools, no element picking. This bundle exists so the Web UI gets a real
browser, not a fram

agent tools, no element picking. This bundle exists so the Web UI gets a real
browser, not a frame.

Everything ships as one installable DSH plugin bundle (`dsh-browser-sidepanel`): a Host half that
ow
ns Chrome and the transport, and a Client half that renders the Sidebar tab.
## How it differs from the Browser that ships with DSH
| | this bundle (`dsh-browser-sidepanel`) | shipped `ui-sidebar-browser` |
| Carrier | real Chrome on the host, driven over CDP | Web: sandboxed `<iframe>`; Desktop: Electron

`<webview>` |
| In the Web GUI | the target — a full browser in the right Sidebar | off by default i

n Web profiles |
[该节后续省略]
## What it does

- **Browser tab in the right Sidebar** — the guide card sits next to *Workspace files* and
*New term

inal*. The tab keeps its page (and canvas) mounted across tab switches, collapse,
and Session switch

es.
- **Real Chrome, not an iframe** — every Session gets its own lazily-launched Chrome with a
temp

orary profile. That means arbitrary sites, logins, SPAs, and sites that refuse framing.
The page is

streamed as JPEG frames over SSE; CDP never reaches the browser.
- **Full interaction** — pointer, w

heel, and keyboard (printable text via `Input.insertText`,
control keys via `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`

), address bar with navigation, back/forward/reload,
multiple tabs, viewport resize. `--headless=new

` by default; set `headless: false` to watch
the real window. The address bar is usable during a col

d start: a URL submitted while Chrome is
still launching is held and navigated as soon as the first

page exists.
- **Pointer feedback** — moving the mouse in the panel shows a pointer dot, draws an an

imated
hover outline around the element under the cursor with its selector caption, and mirrors the

page's own CSS cursor (`pointer`, `text`, `grab`, …), so it is obvious when the page reacts.
- **Ele

ment picking** — press the pick toggle, hover to outline the element under the cursor,
click it, and

the element is captured: unique CSS selector, tag/id/classes, role and
accessible name, text, bound

ing box, selected attributes, up to four ancestors, and a
trimmed `outerHTML`.
- **Mention in the co

mposer** — the `@` button on a pick chip inserts a visible
`@browser #save-btn "Save changes"` token

into the message draft, so you can see (and edit)
what is attached before sending. The full descrip

tor is still attached automatically by the
Host, and the token is plain text, not an atomic `@file`

chip (see limitations).
- **Element into context** — each pick is injected into the owning Session a

s a user-role
context message (`source: {kind: 'browser-panel', form: 'notice'}`), so it reaches the

model
at the next step / next message. Picks are listed as chips in the panel until sent and can be

removed individually or cleared.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness Web profile (`dsh web`) ≥ 0.2.0, Node ≥ 22 (global `WebSocket`/`fetch`).
- A Chro

me/Chromium executable. Default `/usr/bin/google-chrome`; override with
`chromeExecutable` in the ro

um executable. Default `/usr/bin/google-chrome`; override with
`chromeExecutable` in the row config.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Transport**: three same-origin HTTP routes registered on the Host web server, guarded by
`ctx.co

nnection.requestRejection` (the GUI's `dsh-auth-*` cookie). SSE is used for the frame
stream because

the Host web server exempts `text/event-stream` from gzip; a static page is
kept alive with ≤2 fps

JPEG `keepalive` frames.
- **Coordinates**: frames are sent with the CSS viewport they were captured

at, and the client
maps pointer positions with `css = client * viewport / canvas` before dispatchin

g CDP input.
The denominator is Chrome's `metadata.deviceWidth/Height` (= `innerWidth/innerHeight`,

scrollbar included), not `cssVisualViewport` — that distinction is what makes clicks land
exactly.
-

**Lifecycle**: one Chrome per Session, one target per panel tab, lazily launched on first use,
kill

ed via its process group on tab close, Session dispose, plugin dispose, or idle reaper.
- **No npm d

ependencies, no build step**: the Host half imports Node builtins only; the Client
artifact is a sin

gle `window.__ModuleLoader__.load(...)` module that requires only `react`
and uses the DSH theme tok

`window.__ModuleLoader__.load(...)` module that requires only `react`
and uses the DSH theme tokens.
## Limitations and notes

- **Reference chips in the composer are not public DSH API.** A pick shows as a chip inside the
pane

l and is injected as Session context automatically; the `@` chip button inserts a
*plain-text* `@bro

wser <selector> "<text>"` mention through the public `InputActions.insertText`
API, not an `@file`-s

tyle atomic chip.
- Auth is the GUI cookie, so the routes only answer the authenticated page; there

is no token
handshake to configure.
- Headful Chrome works on this host but prints harmlessly about

VA-API/Wayland-Vulkan.
- Sites with heavy bot protection may still dislike an automated Chrome; the

plugin sends no
automation flags by default.
- Editing `client.js` needs a page refresh (or a plugin

toggle) to load; editing `host/`
needs only a `plugin_manager set_plugin` off/on, because `index.js

` stages a fresh module
generation per activation.
